predecessors.name: Warring States Japan
predecessors.text: Nagoya and Kiyosu in Owari, the domain Nobunaga inherited

ledger.x: 1551: Nobunaga heads the Oda, succeeding Oda Nobuhide, who 'died unexpectedly'.
1559: 'After capturing Iwakura Castle, he established his uncontested rule in Owari Province.'

1567: Mino. 'After the siege of Inabayama, he renames the castle and town Gifu'; the Oda clan page lists the Saitō among the clans he dominated; the Azuchi–Momoyama page says he conquered 'the neighboring Mino Province' before the march on Kyoto.
1567-1568: Takigawa Kazumasu 'served in the vanguard of the Oda army for two invasions of Ise Province in 1567 and 1568'.
9 Nov 1568: Kyoto entered; the 'Rokkaku clan in southern Ōmi' driven out; the Azuchi–Momoyama page has him rout the Rokkaku in southern Ōmi on his march.

9 Nov 1568: 'Nobunaga entered Kyoto,' installing Ashikaga Yoshiaki as shogun; the Sengoku page: his march forced Matsunaga Hisahide to relinquish control of the city; the Azuchi–Momoyama page has the Miyoshi withdraw to Settsu.
1568: Hisahide 'forced to submit' after Nobunaga captured Kyoto; the page says he kept Yamato and served Nobunaga.
Early 1570: Nobunaga 'marches on the Asakura clan's domain in Echizen'.
July 1570: he 'besieges Odani Castle in Ōmi Province', the Azai campaign.
August 1570: the Ishiyama Hongan-ji War begins; Nagashima follows in 1571.
1573: 'the end of Azai and Asakura clans'.
1573: after the Azai, Nobunaga 'appointed Hideyoshi daimyō of three districts in the northern part of Ōmi Province'.
1573: the Asakura end.
1573: Echizen after the Asakura.
1577: the Chūgoku campaign (1577-1582) under Hideyoshi, who 'was sent to conquer the Chūgoku region from the Mōri'; the Nobunaga page gives both 1577 and 1578.
19 Nov 1577: Hisahide died at Shigisan after Nobunaga besieged it.
Nov 1577: Yamato.
1579: 'After Tanba was pacified' (the 1578 reward: Kameyama and Tanba Province, 550,000 koku).
1579 (the clan division's year): 'Oda Nobunaga's generals take Uesugi lands in Kaga, Noto and Etchū'.
6-7 Oct 1579: the first Tenshō Iga War (Oda Nobukatsu, Takigawa Kazumasu and others), an Iga victory.
1580: Miki Castle in Harima 'fell to the Oda' (Siege of Miki, 1578-1580); Hideyoshi had entered Harima in late 1576 and the Akamatsu, Bessho and Kodera submitted.
August 1580: 'The fighting finally ended'; Kennyo and his son surrendered, Nobunaga burned the fortress.
August 1580: the Ishiyama site (Osaka); the page lists no territory gained and does not name Settsu, so the circle is the researcher's reading.
8 Oct 1581: the second Tenshō Iga War ends in an Oda victory.
30 Sept to 8 Oct 1581: 'Iga Province brought under' Oda control.
1582: Takigawa Kazumasu 'appointed Kantō-kanrei' with 'a portion of Kōzuke Province as his domain' to watch the Hōjō; he 'lost in the Battle of Kanagawa (1582) against Hōjō' after Nobunaga's death.
1582: 'Nobutada and Ieyasu conquered Shinano and Kai Province', Katsuyori dying after Tenmokuzan.
3 June 1582: Oda forces defeat Kagekatsu at Tenjinyama in Etchū and Uozu Castle falls; the page does not say how much of Etchū the Oda held.
June 1582: Nobunaga killed at Honnō-ji 'during the siege of Takamatsu'; Hideyoshi 'then made peace with the Mōri clan'; the peace is Hideyoshi's, the Oda are ended.
21 June 1582: Akechi Mitsuhide, 'leading 13,000 soldiers', attacks Honnō-ji; Nobunaga dies; Yamazaki 'two weeks later'.

wars.name: Battle of Okehazama
wars.outcome: Imagawa Yoshimoto was killed at Dengaku-Kazama in June 1560; no land changed on the pages.

wars.name: Siege of Inabayama
wars.outcome: The Mino Triumvirate changed sides and Inabayama fell; Nobunaga renamed the castle and town Gifu.

wars.name: Oda campaign against the Azai and Asakura
wars.outcome: Odani (July 1570) and Ichijōdani (1573); 'the end of Azai and Asakura clans' in 1573.

wars.name: Ishiyama Hongan-ji War
wars.outcome: Eleven years of siege; Nagashima fell in 1574 after sieges in 1571 and 1574; the fortress surrendered in August 1580 and was burned.

wars.name: Oda campaign in Tanba and Harima
wars.outcome: Tanba pacified by 1579 under Akechi Mitsuhide; Miki fell in 1580 to Hideyoshi.

wars.name: Chūgoku campaign against the Mōri
wars.outcome: Miki (1578), Tottori (1581) and Takamatsu (1582); Hideyoshi made peace with the Mōri after Honnō-ji.

wars.name: Battle of Nagashino
wars.outcome: Oda and Tokugawa defeated Takeda Katsuyori; no land changed at once (Sengoku page, Nobunaga page).

wars.name: Oda–Uesugi war in Etchū, Noto and Kaga
wars.outcome: Kenshin took Noto and Kaga in 1577 (Tedorigawa, Kaga); Oda generals took Uesugi lands in 1579 and Uozu fell on 3 June 1582.

wars.name: Tenshō Iga War
wars.outcome: Iga victory in 1579; Oda victory in September-October 1581, Iga brought under Oda control.

wars.name: Oda–Tokugawa invasion of Kai
wars.outcome: Nobutada and Ieyasu conquered Shinano and Kai; Katsuyori died at Tenmokuzan on 11 March 1582.

wars.name: Honnō-ji Incident
wars.outcome: Nobunaga died on 21 June 1582; Hideyoshi avenged him at Yamazaki two weeks later.

certainty.note: The pages name castles and provinces, not borders; the Kinai provinces are not named on any page opened, so the 1568-1582 shape under-draws the Oda land.
